rationale: C23 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child letter. Both are presidential letters encouraging civilian support for peacetime armed-forces personnel, and both emphasize the forces' youthful, civilian character and the role of private voluntary and religious organizations. The child substantially adapts C23's rationale—young civilian volunteers should receive visible community support—into a broader appeal for religious and recreational programs near military installations. C22 is closely connected administratively and supplies the Committee's mission, but its executive-order structure is less like the child's letter. C19 offers only a more general appeal to religiously diverse civic participation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The predominantly youthful and civilian character of our large peacetime armed forces makes it imperative that all sections of the community join these programs.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: For the most part, our armed forces are civilian volunteers. Most of them—six out of ten—are under 20 years of age.
shared_material.explanation: The child closely recasts C23's distinctive description of peacetime forces as predominantly young and civilian to justify public support.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I heartily approve the present efforts ... to stimulate community organization on behalf of the men and women of our armed forces.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: We can show them our gratitude through our wholehearted support of the USO.
shared_material.explanation: Both letters endorse organized civilian support for individual service members.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Committee, with the help of the large private voluntary agencies, is going to take its program to the people in communities near military installations
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the six great voluntary agencies which ran USO through the war years, and which broadly represent the three main religious groupings of our citizens, will again be channels for the USO activities
shared_material.explanation: Both rely on large private voluntary agencies, particularly religiously representative ones, as channels for welfare activities serving armed-forces personnel.
